title: The Board of Peace proposes a six-month, 2.45 billion dollar plan to begin Gaza reconstruction
body:
On 23 September 2026, the US-backed Board of Peace proposed a six-month, 2.45 billion dollar plan to start reconstruction and governance in Gaza, the Associated Press reported. Governors unveiled the plan at a board meeting. It contains 66 projects covering infrastructure, education and health, intended to support President Donald Trump's 20-point plan to end the Israel-Hamas war. The board estimated full reconstruction at about 35.2 billion dollars over the medium term and 71.4 billion dollars over the next ten years, saying the need was immense.

The broader plan called for further Israeli military withdrawals, Hamas disarmament, an international peacekeeping force and a new apolitical Palestinian government. The AP said it had largely stalled: Israel's military had expanded its control and now occupied about 60 percent of Gaza, Hamas had not given up its weapons, and the international force and new government had not entered Gaza. Reconstruction had not started and most Palestinians still lived in tent camps or in ruins.

Board high representative Nickolay Mladenov said progress depended largely on Hamas disarming, which the group had refused to do, and urged Israel to scale back its military operation. The board still had to set timelines for deploying the international force and the new government, plans for disarmament, and arrangements for getting building materials into Gaza.
